page: Amazon Web Services c5n.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Vector acceleration instructions include AVX and AVX-512F. System memory totals 10.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, which equates to 2.62 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. It contains no bundled local disk storage, necessitating remote EBS volume attachments, and does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the lower tier of multi-core compute throughput, consistent with its dual-core physical topology. Synthetic testing via stress-ng yields a multi-core score of 3689.06, while Geekbench records scores of 1133.0 in single-core and 2509.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth measurements show 25.89 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 23.10 GB/sec for uncached writes. Operational benchmarks register 3.68 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving capacity of 3.82 GB/sec. Small-scale model inference using a 135M parameter model achieves 75.07 tokens per second during text generation.

The primary architectural tradeoff for the c5n.xlarge involves its dated Skylake-era processing efficiency and reliance entirely on network-attached storage. However, its 2.5:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and 5 Gbps baseline network throughput offer balanced resource allocation for network-sensitive tasks that do not justify heavier compute footprints. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for network routing microservices, API proxy layers, lightweight continuous integration workers, and low-concurrency web application backends.
